neighbours.label: the token ' just' directly after a coordinating 'and' or 'or' ('…, or just sit', '… and just being there'), not ' just' elsewhere
fire: On Sundays we go for a long walk, or just stay in and read the papers.
He talked about his travels and his work and just everything that came to mind.
You can pay by card, by cheque, or just bring cash on the day.
She enjoyed the food and the company and just sitting in the sun.
Whether you want a full meal, a snack, or just a coffee, the café is open.
They laughed about the old days and just forgot the time.
Call me, send a note, or just drop by when you are in town.
The kids ran around the garden and just had a wonderful afternoon.
quiet: On Sundays we had just come back from a long walk when the phone rang.
He has just finished talking about his travels and his work.
It was just a card, but it meant a great deal to her.
She enjoyed the food and the company and loved sitting in the sun.
Whether you want a full meal, a snack, or only a coffee, the café is open.
The old days were just as funny as they remembered.
Just call me or send a note when you are in town.
The kids had just run into the garden when it began to rain.

notes: Card: all 32 top examples peak on ' just', each after 'and'/'or'. Probes: 'or just'/'and just' 0.46-0.58; 'had just arrived' 0.02, 'was just a' 0.06, sentence-initial 'Just' 0.07. 'and simply' also scored 0.39, so the pole may be about a restrictive adverb opening a conjunct, not the word alone; the 'or only' near miss checks that.
